A.explanation: Distance $L$ is half a wavelength, so $\lambda = 2L$ and $f = v/\lambda = v/(2L)$.

B.explanation: This treats $L$ as one full wavelength, but P at a compression to Q at a rarefaction is only half a wavelength.

C.explanation: This is twice the correct frequency and corresponds to treating $L$ as two wavelengths.

D.explanation: This has units of time, not frequency, and is the inverse of the wave equation result.

hints: Look at the crowding of dots: P is in a crowded compression region while Q is in a widely spaced rarefaction region.
Recall that the distance from a compression centre to the next rarefaction centre along a longitudinal wave is half a wavelength.
Use $v = f\lambda$ with $\lambda$ expressed in terms of $L$ to get $f$ in terms of $v$ and $L$.
walkthrough: Identify the pattern in the dot diagram: closely spaced particles mark a compression and widely spaced particles mark a rarefaction.
P lies at a compression and Q lies at the next rarefaction, so the separation $L$ is from maximum compression to maximum rarefaction.
For a longitudinal progressive wave, compression to adjacent rarefaction is half a cycle, so $L = \lambda/2$.
Apply the wave equation $v = f\lambda$, so $f = v/\lambda$.
Substitute $\lambda = 2L$ to get $f = v/(2L)$. This is option A.
